transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-08-31
- Time: 16:00 PT
- Duration: 45 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Evan Torres (Redwood CSM); Carlos Mendez (MedShift CTO), Aisha Khan (ML Eng), Ravi Patel (DevOps), Mei Lin (Product)

Auto-generated summary: Weekly POC sync — onboarding and env readiness, access blockers noted.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining on a Tuesday afternoon, we'll keep to 45. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Carlos: Carlos here.
[00:08] Aisha: Aisha here.
[00:10] Ravi: Ravi on devops.
[00:12] Mei: Mei here.
[00:14] Jordan: Great, Jordan, Priya and Evan from Redwood. We'll do a quick onboarding check, then review the initial inference results you shared and sync on tuning plan.

[02:00] Priya: Quick note — saw the sample logs, thanks Aisha. Some of the prompts are quite long; that affects KV cache behavior and latency numbers. When you say long, you mean like 800 to 1,200 tokens?
[02:12] Aisha: Yeah, most conversation histories are 600-1,000 tokens; the support threads get longer.

[04:30] Priya: Ok that explains the latency bump. For the hosted path we can use prefix caching but on dedicated we get more control over batch windows and sequence length optimization. Also, just FYI I saw a small transcription hiccup in your spreadsheet — 'K-V cash' instead of KV cache, ha.
[04:45] Carlos: (laughs) thanks, we keep typos. Important for us is data residency — we need logs not to leave our VPC for the pilot.
[04:55] Jordan: Understood. The Private deployment supports a customer-managed control plane and KMS integration; we can ensure logs/audit are retained in your region. We'll attach the SOC2 appendix to the deck.

[07:10] Ravi: On peering, we opened the request last week but need Redwood's peering CIDR — what's the next step?
[07:18] Evan: I sent a template earlier; I can resend. For peering we need your CIDR ranges and we will provide the Redwood egress CIDR block. Note that if you want private endpoints for KMS we need to exchange the internal DNS mapping as well.

[09:20] Mei: How long does the SSO/SAML setup usually take? We want to test SSO for the console access.
[09:28] Jordan: Typically 1–2 days once you share the IdP metadata; we'll set up a test connection in our staging account. If you have a jump host policy we can follow that.

[11:40] Priya: Shifting to results — Aisha shared a CSV with 200 inference samples. Quick high-level: baseline model (open LLM vX) on hosted produced median latency 420ms for short prompts, but when prompt length >600 tokens we saw 1.2–1.5s. On our dedicated baseline (small pilot pool) tail latencies were higher due to batching misalignment.
[12:02] Aisha: Right, we saw cost per 1k tokens a bit higher than expected on hosted — we were hoping quantization would help.
[12:18] Priya: It should. Our plan: run 8-bit quantization + CPU offload for certain layers and test quality regression on your three main prompt sets. If quality stays within your threshold (we suggested 2-3% ROUGE-like drop or less for your task), the cost delta will be substantial — roughly 30–40% lower per-token on dedicated.
[13:35] Carlos: What's the tradeoff on latency when you quantize? We've got tight UI SLOs — 500ms median end-to-end.
[13:44] Priya: For short prompts quantization often helps; for long sequences there's a small slow-down in some kernels, but with the right CUDA kernel selection and batch sizing we can hit sub-500ms at median on dedicated hardware. We'll need to test with your real traffic shape.

[16:00] Speaker 2: Can we do throughput and latency bench, like 10k tokens?
[16:05] Priya: Yes, I'll run a 10k-token latency/throughput run on the dedicated pool once peering and KMS access are done — expected results by next Tuesday.

[18:00] Ravi: KMS — we need to check permissions. Do you require key usage or full key admin from our side?
[18:10] Jordan: For private deploy we need a key that the runtime can use for encrypting model cache/ledgers; we don't need admin access. We support customer-managed keys (CMK) in AWS and can integrate with HSM if needed. I'll share a permissions checklist.

[20:35] Aisha: A couple of example failure cases: hallucinations on legal disclaimers, and sometimes outputs are truncated mid-sentence. Any quick mitigation?
[20:48] Priya: For truncation, check max_new_tokens and also the tokenization boundary behavior; we can bump response window and use streaming to avoid UI truncation. For hallucination, that's more prompt engineering — we can add grounding instructions and use reranking or a smaller guidance model for verification. We'll set up an eval harness to measure hallucination rate on your labeled set.

[23:15] Mei: For the pilot success criteria — we need median latency <500ms, 99th <1.2s for core flows, cost per 1k tokens under $X threshold, and SSO + peering in place. Are we aligned?
[23:28] Jordan: Yes, that's sensible. We'll map each criterion to a task owner in the next steps.

[25:40] Carlos: Any red flags on compliance? We require SOC2 plus some ISO pieces.
[25:48] Evan: We are SOC2 Type II, and we have a compliance pack. There may be a few ISO docs we can provide; I'll follow up to collect what you need.

[27:30] Priya: Quick technical deep-dive point — your sequence distribution has spikes at >1,000 tokens; that drives KV cache thrash. Two immediate levers: 1) truncate older context and store vectorized summaries in long-term store, 2) aggressively use prefix caching for hosted. We'll prototype both for you.
[28:05] Aisha: The team prefers to keep full convo history for cases so maybe summaries could work.

[30:00] Jordan: On billing/commits — if you go Dedicated with reserved capacity we can show committed cost vs burst pricing. I'll prepare scenarios (monthly commit levels).
[30:20] Carlos: Is there an uplift for guaranteed latency SLO?
[30:25] Jordan: There can be tiers — higher committed capacity and pre-warmed nodes improve SLOs; we'll include those options in the cost scenarios.

[33:10] Priya: I'll run 3 experiments: (A) baseline no quant, (B) 8-bit quant, (C) 8-bit quant + kernel tuning. We'll measure latency, cost, and a small quality score on your labels. Expect results by next Wednesday.
[33:28] Aisha: Sounds good. Also we have some golden examples for hallucination checks — I'll drop those in the shared drive.

[35:00] Ravi: Small infra note — our security team requires that the peering is initiated from our side. We'll need your egress CIDR and the ASN if you're using a transit gateway.
[35:12] Evan: We'll provide the egress CIDR and ASN. Also note if you want VPC endpoints for KMS we need to exchange the endpoint ARNs.

[37:40] Mei: Timeline check — when would a short pilot benchmark happen?
[37:46] Priya: As soon as peering + KMS access are done. If infra completes by 2027-09-02 we can run benchmarks 2027-09-05 through 2027-09-07.

[39:50] Jordan: Let's recap quick — Action owners: Jordan sends pricing and SOC2 appendix; Priya runs quantization and kernel experiments and shares results; Ravi to complete peering; Aisha to share prompt sets and golden examples; Evan to send peering template and egress info.
[40:10] Carlos: Ok agreed. Anything else?
[40:18] Mei: Can Redwood share a short runbook for onboarding steps? A checklist would help our infra team.
[40:24] Jordan: Yes, we'll share a runbook and a one-page access checklist today.

[42:00] Speaker 1: Quick question from chat — will the dedicated pool support autoscaling?
[42:07] Priya: Yes, dedicated supports autoscaling with configurable policies and burst capacity; we'll show recommended settings for your workload.

[43:00] Jordan: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up on items. Next sync same time next week?
[43:08] Carlos: Works for us.
[43:12] Jordan: Great, meeting adjourned.

End of transcript.

Attachments/refs: shared drive link to sample prompts (link redacted), initial results CSV referenced by Aisha (file: medshift_inference_samples_v1.csv), cost scenarios doc (to be attached by Jordan).
